title: Homeowner Heat Pump FAQs - Efficiency Maine
summary: Efficiency Maine's homeowner FAQ on heat pump cold performance, bills, emissions, refrigerant and rebates.

assertions.quote: Properly sized, selected, and located heat pumps can heat a home without backup.
Many heat pumps provide efficient heating down to -22°F or lower, regardless of windchill.
heating with heat pumps is usually less expensive than heating with oil, kerosene, or propane
it would have less global warming potential than running an oil or gas boiler or furnace for a year

verdicts.note: A 2-5 lb R-410A charge is about 2-5 tCO2e, comparable to a gas furnace's annual emissions and below a typical oil boiler's.

assertions.quote: Heat pumps cool for half the cost of window air conditioners.

verdicts.note: Inverter mini-splits have seasonal efficiency ratings roughly twice those of typical window units.
Cooling-only mini-splits replacing room ACs save about 156 kWh per ton a year in MA, a modest saving that does not make the upgrade cost-effective (benefit-cost 0.16).
Against an EER 9.8 window AC baseline, the average mini-split saved about 54 kWh per summer (213 vs 159 kWh), a modest but real saving.
Heat pumps cool more efficiently than window and portable air conditioners (secondary citation); the passage does not single out ductless units.
